correctness.rationale: For squarefree n the two normalized functions are the sum of reciprocals and the product of one-minus-reciprocals. For even n>2 the term n/2 alone is odd, while φ(n) is even; for odd n>1 with odd support every n/p is odd and φ(n) is even. The empty support fails and the one-prime equation gives 2; for two odd primes (p−2)(q−2)=3 gives exactly 15. At four odd primes F>0 is necessary and solving the one remaining reciprocal gives exactly the displayed s; 0<1/s<1/r yields the strict bounds in the proof. Independently, the normalized product-minus-sum gap strictly increases with each prime variable, and even the lower benchmarks (5,11,13,15), (5,7,11,13), (3,17,19,21) and (3,13,17,19) have positive gap, excluding their entire ordered ranges. The pair (3,5) already has zero gap before adding more primes, so it cannot give equality after adding two. For the remaining pairs (3,7) and (3,11), repeating r in the fourth position gives the strict bound r<2(1+T)/F; positivity of the three-variable gap gives the lower bound. Exact rational replay gives s=549,123,747/13,189/5,1011/29,669/25,881/49. The integers are divisible by 3 and the others are nonintegral. The unbounded exclusions and the odd-support parity, not a finite interval in n, establish the barrier.
residual_risks: No assertion on the existence of support-six or higher solutions, or on nonsquarefree numbers.
